2. Carbo destructionis, omnia incendens, & in cineres
redigens, cernebatur abhinc: à quo enim Judæi
in suâ infidelitate sese exhibuerunt obfirmatos & incu-
rabiles, Dux ecclesiæ non solùm suos eduxit ex Synagogâ
Judaicâ, & credentes Pellam concedere jussit;
verùm etiam omnem suam defensionem ab istâ Republicâ
auferens, post se abiurientem judicium deflagratio-
nis, quæ totam illam terram devastavit, reliquit; quod
judicium exsequi cœpit divina vindicta (terram, ante
in hæreditatem datam, anathemate percutiens) sub finem
imperii Neronis, quandò Vespasiano contra gentem
Judaicam, ad arma confugientem, missò, & in pœnam
rebellantium totam Galilæam miserè vastante, prima
viderunt incendia, præstantissimas civitates, lætissimasque
regiones planè absumentia: indè armis in Judæam
circumlatis validissima oppida iterum in potestatem suam
redacta subvertit hostis, non subsistens, donec caput
gentis Hierosolymas aggrederetur: cujus obsidio, propter
Neronis aliorumque Principum cædem quidem ad
tempus interrupta, mox tamen eo cum rerum eventu
instaurata fuit, ut occupata civitas Judaicæ genti ac nomini
exitium intulerit, quippe quæ à victoribus subversa
& planè solo æquata, pabulum voracibus flammis
facta, disparuit: quæ eadem reliquorum munimentorum
sors cùm fuerit, nihil ab isto carbone non destructum
remansit.

page.notes: The text runs to the foot of the page, and the last line ends in "cerat" after a printed hyphen. Long s is transcribed as s throughout, so the printed forms "compofuiffe", "destructionis", "absumentia", "subsistens" and "exsequi" appear here as composuisse, destructionis, absumentia, subsistens and exsequi. The reference line "CAP. III: 3. b.9. a" at the head is a reference marker and is not part of the running head. Ink specks and a blot near the foot and along the edges are stains, not text, and have been left out. No signature or catchword is visible.
